findings.current: Behind them stood someone with a conical hat pulled low over their face.
findings.defect: The source says only that someone was there; it does not establish that the person stood behind the monks.
findings.rationale: The added location changes the physical staging without support from the Korean.
findings.replacement: There stood someone wearing a conical hat pulled low over their face.

findings.current: They were the last people he wanted to meet, especially now, when his simple-minded subordinate had killed someone in the middle of a main road.
findings.defect: “The last people he wanted to meet” makes his reaction stronger than the source’s description of them as an awkward or difficult opponent to encounter.
findings.rationale: 마주치기 껄끄러운 상대 describes an uncomfortable or difficult encounter, not necessarily the people he least wanted to meet.
findings.replacement: They were an awkward group to run into, especially now, when his simple-minded subordinate had killed someone in the middle of a main road.

findings.current: The Murim was full of masters far above his level. To know this much about a man like Blood Cudgel suggested an intelligence network woven as tightly as a spiderweb.
findings.defect: “Suggested” weakens the source’s explicit statement that this degree of knowledge was evidence of a densely woven intelligence network.
findings.rationale: The Korean says this knowledge “was evidence” (증거였다), rather than merely suggesting the network’s existence.
findings.replacement: The Murim was full of masters far above his level. To know this much about a man like Blood Cudgel was proof of an intelligence network woven as tightly as a spiderweb.

findings.current: He was displeased that this had happened, and he was not particularly impressed by the attitude of the Black Dragon Demon Gate’s Young Sect Leader, whose reputation he had already heard.
findings.defect: The assembled copy omits the detail that Jung Ho, though a martial monk, had spent many years at Shaolin following the Buddhist path. The accepted baseline preserved it.
findings.rationale: The source explicitly gives Jung Ho’s long Buddhist practice as context before describing his displeasure; the detail is absent from the assembled copy.
findings.replacement: Though he was a martial monk, he had spent many years at Shaolin walking the path of a Buddhist. He was displeased that this had happened, and he was not particularly impressed by the attitude of the Black Dragon Demon Gate’s Young Sect Leader, whose reputation he had already heard.

summary: The translation is largely faithful, but it adds a spatial detail, slightly intensifies one reaction, weakens a stated inference, and omits a source detail preserved in the accepted baseline.
